tldr: This is a research-theme thread, not one event: through October and early November, papers reworked deep research agents around iterative state, video sources and page-image input. On Nov 12 and Nov 25 the focus moved to multi-agent coordination and to scoring report coverage.
whats_new: On Nov 27, Shandu 4.0 shipped as an open-source local deep research agent that checks every cited sentence against its source text, with any LiteLLM-supported model.
why_it_matters: Deep research is moving from demos to measurable systems: coordination cost, rubric-scored coverage and per-sentence citation checks are now concrete things to evaluate in your own research agent.

status.detail: Loosely linked work on how deep research agents split work, get scored and prove their citations.

beats.headline: Multi-agent deep research: delegation pays off only when it is coordinated
beats.summary: Delegation parallelizes search and keeps long tool traces out of the main agent's context, but only helps when allocation and execution line up.

beats.headline: DRBench Pro scores report coverage; best agent reaches 57.04%
beats.summary: 144 cases and 44,102 rubrics built from Wikipedia-derived knowledge trees.

beats.headline: Shandu 4.0: a local open-source agent that audits every citation
beats.summary: CLI and web UI over web, arXiv, PubMed and PDF search, with each cited sentence checked against its source.

open_questions: Does Shandu's citation audit catch unsupported claims that DRBench Pro-style coverage rubrics miss?
Will any multi-agent deep research system report a DRBench Pro score above 57.04%?
What token or latency overhead does coordinated multi-agent delegation add over a single agent?
Do page-image (vision-language) inputs from earlier work raise coverage on benchmarks like DRBench Pro?
take_for_builders: If you ship a research agent, add a per-sentence citation check against retrieved source text before release, and score report coverage with rubrics instead of judging fluency.

day_captions.e267de687efb45c3: Frames the multi-agent design problem: delegation saves main-agent context but fails without coordinated task allocation.
day_captions.b771eb023b90c8cb: Adds a coverage benchmark with a hard number: the best agent covers 57.04% of rubric knowledge.
day_captions.0fe8a1f1febc51fc: First practitioner tool in the thread: runs locally and verifies citations sentence by sentence.
